L29: # Homomorphisms of Hecke–Kiselman Monoids Associated to Simple Oriented Graphs
L30: 
L31: Luka Andrenšek Email: andrensek.luka@gmail.com Affiliation: Department of Mathematics, Faculty of Mathematics and Physics, University of Ljubljana, Jadranska ulica 19, Ljubljana, SI-1000, Slovenia
L32: ###### Abstract
L33: 
L34: Let $\Gamma$ and $\Theta$ be finite simple oriented graphs, and let $\mathbf{HK}_{\Gamma}$ and $\mathbf{HK}_{\Theta}$ denote the corresponding Hecke–Kiselman monoids. We present a set of Boolean matrices that is in bijection with the set of monoid homomorphisms from $\mathbf{HK}_{\Gamma}$ to $\mathbf{HK}_{\Theta}$. In particular, we obtain a Boolean matrix monoid isomorphic to the endomorphism monoid of $\mathbf{HK}_{\Theta}$.
L35: ###### keywords
L36: 
L37: Hecke–Kiselman monoid, homomorphism, endomorphism monoid, idempotent, Boolean matrix monoid
L38: ## 1 Introduction
L39: Let $\Theta$ be a finite simple oriented graph, that is, a finite oriented graph with no multiple arrows, no loops, and no oriented cycles of length $2$. Let $V_{\Theta}=\{x_{1},x_{2},\dots,x_{n}\}$ be the vertex set of $\Theta$ for some positive integer $n$. If there is an arrow from $x_{i}$ to $x_{j}$ in $\Theta$, we write $x_{i}\overset{\Theta}{\to}x_{j}$.
L40: For distinct vertices $x_{i}$ and $x_{j}$, we say that $x_{i}$ and $x_{j}$ are not connected in $\Theta$ if there is no arrow from $x_{i}$ to $x_{j}$ and there is no arrow from $x_{j}$ to $x_{i}$ in $\Theta$.
L41: In cite16†Ganyushkin and Mazorchuk (2011) , Ganyushkin and Mazorchuk define the Hecke–Kiselman monoid $\mathbf{HK}_{\Theta}$ associated to $\Theta$ as the monoid generated by
L42: 
L43:  | $$x_{1},x_{2},\dots,x_{n}$$  |
L44: 
L45: subject to the following defining relations for all $x_{i},x_{j}\in V_{\Theta}$:
L46: 
L47:   * •
L48: 
L49: $x_{i}^{2}=x_{i}$;
L50: 
L51:   * •
L52: 
L53: $x_{i}x_{j}=x_{j}x_{i}$ if $x_{i}$ and $x_{j}$ are not connected in $\Theta$;
L54: 
L55:   * •
L56: 
L57: $x_{i}x_{j}x_{i}=x_{j}x_{i}x_{j}=x_{i}x_{j}$ if $x_{i}\overset{\Theta}{\to}x_{j}$.
L58: We denote by $e$ the unit element of $\mathbf{HK}_{\Theta}$. Let $\Gamma$ be another finite simple oriented graph with vertex set $V_{\Gamma}=\{y_{1},y_{2},\dots,y_{m}\}$ for some positive integer $m$, and let $\mathbf{HK}_{\Gamma}$ denote the corresponding Hecke–Kiselman monoid.
L59: This paper studies the set of all monoid homomorphisms from $\mathbf{HK}_{\Gamma}$ to $\mathbf{HK}_{\Theta}$, which we denote by $\mathrm{Hom}(\mathbf{HK}_{\Gamma},\mathbf{HK}_{\Theta})$, and the endomorphism monoid $\mathrm{End}(\mathbf{HK}_{\Theta})$ whose operation is the usual composition of maps. Throughout, monoid homomorphisms are assumed to preserve the identity element.
L60: Hecke–Kiselman monoids were originally introduced in the setting of finite simple digraphs cite16†Ganyushkin and Mazorchuk (2011) . They are a natural mixture of two families of monoids, namely, 0-Hecke monoids, which are closely connected to Coxeter groups, and Kiselman monoids cite17†Kiselman (2002) ; cite18†Kudryavtseva and Mazorchuk (2009) . They have been studied by various authors cite19†Aragona and D’Andrea (2013) ; cite20†Aragona and D’Andrea (2020) ; cite21†Ashikhmin et al.
L61: (2015) ; cite22†Collina and D’Andrea (2015) ; cite23†Forsberg (2017) ; cite16†Ganyushkin and Mazorchuk (2011) ; cite24†Lebed (2025) ; cite25†Wiertel (2024) . Particular interest has been devoted to the corresponding Hecke–Kiselman algebras cite26†Okniński and Wiertel (2020) ; cite27†Okniński and Wiertel (2021) ; cite28†Wiertel (2022) ; cite29†Wiertel (2023) . In this paper, we only consider Hecke–Kiselman monoids associated to simple oriented graphs.
L62: From the proof of (cite16†Ganyushkin and Mazorchuk, 2011 , Theorem 16), it follows that monoid isomorphisms from $\mathbf{HK}_{\Gamma}$ to $\mathbf{HK}_{\Theta}$ are in bijection with graph isomorphisms from $\Gamma$ to $\Theta$. Setting $\Gamma=\Theta$, it can be verified that the automorphism group of $\mathbf{HK}_{\Theta}$ is isomorphic to the automorphism group of the graph $\Theta$.
L63: To the best of our knowledge, general monoid homomorphisms from $\mathbf{HK}_{\Gamma}$ to $\mathbf{HK}_{\Theta}$ and the structure of the endomorphism monoid of $\mathbf{HK}_{\Theta}$ have not been systematically studied in the literature. However, a description of endomorphisms of the Kiselman monoid, which is the Hecke–Kiselman monoid corresponding to the complete acyclic oriented graph, is known in the literature cite30†Andrenšek (2026) .
L64: The main result of this paper is Theorem cite31†4.5 . We show that $\mathrm{Hom}(\mathbf{HK}_{\Gamma},\mathbf{HK}_{\Theta})$ is in bijection with the set of Boolean matrices corresponding to $(\Gamma,\Theta)$-admissible sequences of sets, which are defined in Definition cite32†4.2 .
L65: These are finite sequences of length $m$ of subsets of $V_{\Theta}$ for which the induced full subgraphs of $\Theta$ do not contain any oriented cycles, and which satisfy a simple graph-theoretic condition, later denoted by $p_{\Theta}$ and defined in Definition cite33†3.1 , according to arrows in $\Gamma$.
L66: Furthermore, in Theorem cite34†5.4 , we show that in the case $\Gamma=\Theta$, the constructed bijection between $\mathrm{End}(\mathbf{HK}_{\Theta})$ and the corresponding Boolean matrices is a monoid isomorphism.
L67: The paper is organised as follows. In Section cite7†2 , we establish basic notation and recall results from the relevant literature. In Section cite11†3 , we prove new results on idempotents in $\mathbf{HK}_{\Theta}$. These results are used to prove the main result in Section cite12†4 , and we consider the endomorphism monoid of $\mathbf{HK}_{\Theta}$ in Section cite13†5 .
L68: ## 2 Preliminaries
L69: 
L70: Denote by $F(V_{\Theta})$ the free monoid over the alphabet $V_{\Theta}=\{x_{1},x_{2},\dots,x_{n}\}$. Elements of $F(V_{\Theta})$ are called words, and each $x_{i}\in V_{\Theta}$ is called a letter. In what follows, we will use the term letter to refer to the vertices of $\Theta$, generators of $\mathbf{HK}_{\Theta}$, and generators of $F(V_{\Theta})$. We have the canonical projection
L71: 
L72:  | $$\pi:F(V_{\Theta})\twoheadrightarrow\mathbf{HK}_{\Theta}.$$  |
L73: For a word $w\in F(V_{\Theta})$, denote by $\ell(w)$ its length. The unique word of length $0$ is called the empty word.
L74: ### 2.1 The Content Map
L75: 
L76: For a word $w\in F(V_{\Theta})$, we define its content $c(w)$ as the set of $x_{i}\in V_{\Theta}$ for which $x_{i}$ appears in $w$. Since the defining relations of $\mathbf{HK}_{\Theta}$ preserve content, we can define the content and denote it again by $c(x)$ for $x\in\mathbf{HK}_{\Theta}$ as the content of any word $w\in F(V_{\Theta})$ with $x=\pi(w)$. Moreover, we have
L77: 
L78:  | $$c(xy)=c(x)\cup c(y)\quad\text{and}\quad c(e)=\emptyset,$$  |
L79: which shows that $c:\mathbf{HK}_{\Theta}\twoheadrightarrow\mathbbm{2}^{V_{\Theta}}$ is a monoid epimorphism, where $\mathbbm{2}^{V_{\Theta}}$ is equipped with the operation $\cup$.
L80: 
L81: We use the following lemma in the proof of Proposition cite35†5.1 .
L82: ###### Lemma 2.1.
L83: 
L84: Let $\psi,\varphi\in\mathrm{End}(\mathbf{HK}_{\Theta})$ and $x_{i}\in\mathbf{HK}_{\Theta}$. Then
L85: 
L86:  | $$c((\psi\circ\varphi)(x_{i}))=\bigcup_{x_{j}\in c(\varphi(x_{i}))}c(\psi(x_{j})).$$  |
L87: ###### Proof.
L88: 
L89: If $\varphi(x_{i})=e$, then we have $c(\varphi(x_{i}))=\emptyset$ and $(\psi\circ\varphi)(x_{i})=e$. Hence $c((\psi\circ\varphi)(x_{i}))=\emptyset$, and thus the conclusion holds in this case.
L90: 
L91: Now suppose $\varphi(x_{i})\neq e$ and write $\varphi(x_{i})=x_{i_{1}}\dots x_{i_{k}}$ for some letters $x_{i_{1}},\dots,x_{i_{k}}\in\mathbf{HK}_{\Theta}$ and $k\geq 1$. Then $c(\varphi(x_{i}))=\{x_{i_{1}},\dots,x_{i_{k}}\}$ and we further have
L92:  | $$(\psi\circ\varphi)(x_{i})=\psi(\varphi(x_{i}))=\psi(x_{i_{1}}\dots x_{i_{k}})=\psi(x_{i_{1}})\dots\psi(x_{i_{k}}).$$  |
L93: 
L94: Hence we have
L95: 
L96:  | $$c((\psi\circ\varphi)(x_{i}))=c(\psi(x_{i_{1}}))\cup\dots\cup c(\psi(x_{i_{k}})),$$  |
L97: 
L98: and therefore,
L99: 
L100:  | $$c((\psi\circ\varphi)(x_{i}))=\bigcup_{x_{j}\in\{x_{i_{1}},\dots,x_{i_{k}}\}}c(\psi(x_{j}))=\bigcup_{x_{j}\in c(\varphi(x_{i}))}c(\psi(x_{j})).$$  |
L101: 
L102: ∎
L103: ### 2.2 Normal Forms in $\mathbf{HK}_{\Theta}$
L104: 
L105: Here we recall the main results from cite20†Aragona and D’Andrea (2020) . The following lemma is proved in (cite20†Aragona and D’Andrea, 2020 , Lemma 1).
L106: ###### Lemma 2.2.
L107: 
L108: If $x_{i}\in\mathbf{HK}_{\Theta}$ is a letter and $w\in\mathbf{HK}_{\Theta}$ is obtained by multiplying letters that do not admit arrows to (respectively from) $x_{i}$, then $x_{i}wx_{i}=x_{i}w$ (respectively $x_{i}wx_{i}=wx_{i}$).
L109: 
L110: The right cancellation $\overset{r}{\to}$ and left cancellation $\overset{l}{\to}$ are binary relations on $F(V_{\Theta})$ defined as follows. For $w,w^{\prime}\in F(V_{\Theta})$, we have
L111: 
L112:   * •
L113: $w\overset{r}{\to}w^{\prime}$ if there exist words $w_{1},w_{2},u\in F(V_{\Theta})$, and a letter $x_{i}\in F(V_{\Theta})$ such that $w=w_{1}x_{i}ux_{i}w_{2}$, $w^{\prime}=w_{1}x_{i}uw_{2}$, and no letter in $u$ has an arrow to $x_{i}$.
L114: 
L115:   * •
L116: 
L117: $w\overset{l}{\to}w^{\prime}$ if there exist words $w_{1},w_{2},u\in F(V_{\Theta})$, and a letter $x_{i}\in F(V_{\Theta})$ such that $w=w_{1}x_{i}ux_{i}w_{2}$, $w^{\prime}=w_{1}ux_{i}w_{2}$, and no letter in $u$ has an arrow from $x_{i}$.
L118: Right and left cancellations are also called elementary cancellations. Denote by $\to=\overset{r}{\to}\cup\overset{l}{\to}$ and let $\overset{*}{\to}$ be the reflexive-transitive closure of $\to$ on $F(V_{\Theta})$. Then Lemma cite36†2.2 implies that for $u,v\in F(V_{\Theta})$, if $u\to v$, then $\pi(u)=\pi(v)$. Therefore, if $w\overset{*}{\to}w^{\prime}$ for $w,w^{\prime}\in F(V_{\Theta})$, then $\pi(w)=\pi(w^{\prime})$.
L119: ###### Definition 2.3.
L120: 
L121: A word $w\in F(V_{\Theta})$ is a normal form of $x\in\mathbf{HK}_{\Theta}$ if $x=\pi(w)$ and no elementary cancellations may be performed on $w$.
L122: 
L123: Every $x\in\mathbf{HK}_{\Theta}$ has at least one normal form, as any word of minimal length in $\pi^{-1}(\{x\})$ must be a normal form of $x$. Denote by $\mathcal{N}$ the set of all normal forms of all elements of $\mathbf{HK}_{\Theta}$.
L124: Define the equivalence relation $\sim$ on $F(V_{\Theta})$, which is generated by elementary commutations:
L125: 
L126:  | $$w_{1}x_{i}x_{j}w_{2}\sim w_{1}x_{j}x_{i}w_{2},$$  |
L127: 
L128: for all words $w_{1},w_{2}\in F(V_{\Theta})$, and letters $x_{i},x_{j}\in F(V_{\Theta})$ such that $x_{i}$ and $x_{j}$ are not connected in $\Theta$. The following was proved in (cite20†Aragona and D’Andrea, 2020 , Theorem 1).
L129: ###### Theorem 2.4.
L130: 
L131: The following statements hold.
L132: 
L133:   1. (i)
L134: 
L135: Let $w,w^{\prime}\in F(V_{\Theta})$. If $\pi(w)=\pi(w^{\prime})$ and $u,v\in\mathcal{N}$ satisfy $w\overset{*}{\to}u$ and $w^{\prime}\overset{*}{\to}v$, then $u\sim v$.
L136: 
L137:   2. (ii)
L138: 
L139: Every simplifying sequence
L140: 
L141:  | $$w\to w_{1}\to w_{2}\to\dots\to w_{k}$$  |
L142: 
L143: may be extended to a simplifying sequence ending on a normal form of $\pi(w)$.
L144: ### 2.3 Idempotents in $\mathbf{HK}_{\Theta}$
L145: 
L146: For $X\subseteq V_{\Theta}$, denote by $\Theta[X]$ the full subgraph of $\Theta$ with vertex set $X$, that is, $\Theta[X]$ is an oriented graph with vertex set $X$ and for $x_{i},x_{j}\in X$, there is an arrow from $x_{i}$ to $x_{j}$ in $\Theta[X]$ if and only if there is an arrow from $x_{i}$ to $x_{j}$ in $\Theta$.
L147: 
L148: In (cite23†Forsberg, 2017 , Theorem 3.6), the following theorem is proved for a general finite simple oriented graph $\Theta$.
L149: ###### Theorem 2.5.
L150: 
L151: There is a bijection between idempotents in $\mathbf{HK}_{\Theta}$ and full subgraphs of $\Theta$ which do not contain any oriented cycles.
L152: 
L153: In the proof, an idempotent is mapped to the full subgraph of $\Theta$ whose vertex set is the content of the idempotent. Therefore, for each $X\subseteq V_{\Theta}$ such that $\Theta[X]$ does not contain any oriented cycles, there exists exactly one idempotent in $\mathbf{HK}_{\Theta}$ with content $X$. We denote this idempotent by $e_{X}$.
L154: We denote the following set
L155:
